hero.headline: U.S. shoots down Iranian missiles and drones, strikes targets near Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
U.S. forces shot down multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones and conducted strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to attempted attacks across the Middle East. U.S. Central Command said all Iranian ballistic missiles failed to hit their intended targets, marking a significant escalation in military tensions between the two nations.

According to CENTCOM, two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart during flight, while three missiles launched at Bahrain were intercepted by U.S. and Bahrain air defense forces. The U.S. military characterized these actions as defensive operations necessary to protect American forces and regional partners.

The strikes on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz followed the attempted Iranian attacks. The confrontation extended beyond direct military exchanges, with American forces also responding to Iranian threats aimed at regional allies. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway through which much of the world's oil passes.

In a separate incident, an F-35C fighter jet from the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone in the Arabian Sea. According to Captain Tim Hawkins, a navy spokesperson at Central Command, the drone was "aggressively" approaching the carrier "with unclear intent" when it was intercepted. "An F-35C fighter jet from Abraham Lincoln shot down the Iranian drone in self-defence and to protect the aircraft carrier and personnel on board," Hawkins said. No U.S. service members were harmed or equipment damaged.

Also on Tuesday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards harassed a U.S.-flagged merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Two IRGC boats and an Iranian Mohajer drone approached the M/V Stena Imperative at high speeds and threatened to board the tanker, according to military officials.

These military confrontations come as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran have stalled. However, there are signs negotiations may resume. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian announced he had instructed the country's foreign minister to "pursue fair and equitable negotiations" with the U.S., marking a potential shift in Tehran's position. The White House confirmed that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff plans to hold talks with Iranian officials later in the week.

The escalation represents the latest in a series of military exchanges in the Middle East involving American and Iranian forces. U.S. Central Command oversees military operations across the Middle East and Central Asia, including forces stationed in Kuwait, Bahrain, and other regional bases that came under threat from the Iranian attacks. The deterioration in relations underscores the fragile security situation in the region amid continued tensions over nuclear negotiations and American military presence near Iranian waters.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio testifies on Iran negotiations and foreign policy
cards.teaser: Marco Rubio detailed US demands as peace talks with Iran face obstacles.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared before the Senate to discuss ongoing negotiations with Iran and other foreign policy matters. Rubio outlined specific demands the United States is making as part of peace talks that have encountered significant difficulties.

Senators questioned Rubio on multiple foreign policy issues during the hearing, including Ukraine and Iran. Senator Shaheen criticized Rubio for what she described as ignoring Senate requests for information on these and other international matters.

cards.headline: Russia intensifies Ukraine attacks as public concern grows
cards.teaser: Moscow is increasing military operations more than four years into the war.
cards.body:
Russia is intensifying attacks in Ukraine as the conflict enters its fifth year. Russian forces recently launched a massive aerial assault on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, killing at least 22 civilians and wounding 138 others.

President Putin has maintained an uncompromising stance on the war, showing no signs of pursuing a negotiated settlement. However, public discourse within Russia appears to be shifting, with growing concern about the prolonged conflict visible even among some Putin loyalists after more than four years of sustained military operations.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as partial Hezbollah truce continues
cards.teaser: Israeli forces are conducting operations in the south but have not struck Beirut since a US-announced agreement.
cards.body:
Israel has continued military operations in southern Lebanon while maintaining a partial truce with Hezbollah in other areas. Following a US-announced agreement, Israel has refrained from striking Beirut, the capital.

The arrangement has created a geographic division in Israeli military activity, with active operations persisting in the southern region while the capital remains untargeted under the terms of the deal.

cards.headline: Primary elections underway in six states including California and Iowa
cards.teaser: Voters across the United States are selecting candidates for governor and Congress as polls begin to close.
cards.body:
Primary elections took place in six states including California, Iowa, New Jersey, South Dakota, New Mexico, and Montana. Voters selected candidates for the November midterm elections, with contests determining the final lineup for gubernatorial and congressional seats.

In California, the primary featured races for governor, the Los Angeles mayor position, and congressional seats. The results from these contests will shape the political landscape heading into the midterm campaign season.

cards.headline: Canada urges renewal of North American free-trade agreement
cards.teaser: Canadian officials sent a letter to U.S. and Mexican trade representatives calling for a 16-year extension.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal in a letter from Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc to his U.S. and Mexican counterparts. The request comes amid economic and political pressure from the Trump administration.

The three countries must decide on the future of their trade relationship, which currently governs commerce between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

hero.headline: Canada requests 16-year extension of North American trade agreement
hero.teaser: Canadian trade minister formally asked the US and Mexico to renew the USMCA pact.
hero.body:
Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has formally requested that the three North American countries renew the USMCA trade deal with a 16-year extension. In a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico, LeBlanc called for the renewal of the trade pact that governs commerce between the nations.

The request comes amid ongoing bilateral trade discussions. LeBlanc met with the U.S. Trade Representative on Tuesday to discuss trade issues between the two countries.

cards.headline: South Koreans vote in local elections as test of President Lee
cards.teaser: Voting is underway in municipal races seen as a gauge of support after Lee's first year in office.
cards.body:
South Korea is holding local elections that observers view as the first electoral test for President Lee one year into office. The municipal races are being watched as an indicator of public support for Lee's leadership during the initial year of the presidency.

The local elections will determine leadership in cities and provinces across South Korea. Political analysts are treating the results as a measure of the administration's performance and standing with voters after 12 months in power.

cards.headline: Australia and Solomon Islands agree to negotiate comprehensive treaty
cards.teaser: The two countries plan to negotiate a broader agreement amid questions about Solomon Islands' security arrangements.
cards.body:
Australia and Solomon Islands announced they will negotiate a comprehensive treaty governing their bilateral relationship. The Solomon Islands prime minister said the country would review its security pact with China as part of broader diplomatic discussions.

The negotiations come as Australia seeks to strengthen ties with the Pacific island nation. The security relationship between Solomon Islands and China has been a source of concern for Australian officials and regional observers.

cards.headline: Protests grow in Albania over Kushner-linked resort project
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury developments on the Adriatic Sea have become a flashpoint for frustrations with the government.
cards.body:
Plans for luxury resorts on Albania's Adriatic Sea coast linked to the Kushner family have sparked growing protests. Environmentalists have long worried about the development projects and their potential impact on the coastal region.

The resort plans have become a focal point for broader public frustration with the Albanian government. Demonstrators are using the development issue to express wider discontent with government policies and decision-making.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as partial Hezbollah truce continues
cards.teaser: Israeli forces are conducting operations in the south but have not struck Beirut since a US-announced agreement.
cards.body:
Israel has continued military operations in southern Lebanon while maintaining a partial truce with Hezbollah in other areas. Following a US-announced agreement, Israel has refrained from striking Beirut, the capital.

The arrangement has created a geographic division in Israeli military activity, with active operations persisting in the southern region while the capital remains untargeted under the terms of the deal.

cards.headline: Court delays US Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya
cards.teaser: A ruling further postpones the Trump administration's proposed unit for Americans exposed to the virus.
cards.body:
A court ruling has further delayed the Trump administration's plans to establish an Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to the virus.

Residents of Nanyuki, the town near the proposed site at Laikipia Air Base, have voiced strong opposition to the plan. Local people argue the facility poses a health risk to their community, particularly since Kenya has no known Ebola cases. Critics also view the proposal as a double standard, suggesting Americans should quarantine in their home country rather than potentially expose Kenyans to disease.

hero.headline: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use Republican-favored congressional map
hero.teaser: The ruling permits Alabama to proceed with elections using six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.
hero.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that Alabama can implement a redrawn congressional map for the 2026 midterm elections. The new map creates six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.

The decision eliminates one of Alabama's two majority-Black districts, representing a significant loss for Black voters. The ruling comes after a lengthy legal battle over the state's congressional boundaries and follows the Court's April decision that made it much harder to challenge voting maps under the Voting Rights Act.

cards.headline: Trump administration drops $1.8 billion compensation fund after Republican pushback
cards.teaser: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision to abandon the fund amid opposition from top GOP lawmakers.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has abandoned a planned $1.8 billion compensation fund following opposition from Republican lawmakers. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision to set aside the fund, which was described as an "anti-weaponisation" initiative.

The reversal came after top GOP lawmakers raised objections to the program, prompting the administration to reverse course on the initiative.

cards.headline: Primary elections underway in six states including California and Iowa
cards.teaser: Voters across the United States are selecting candidates for governor and Congress as polls begin to close.
cards.body:
Primary elections took place in six states including California, Iowa, New Jersey, South Dakota, New Mexico, and Montana. Voters selected candidates for the November midterm elections, with contests determining the final lineup for gubernatorial and congressional seats.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner meets with Democrats amid texting scandal
cards.teaser: Senate Democrats huddled with the candidate after reports emerged of sexually explicit texts.
cards.body:
Graham Platner met with key Democratic leaders in Washington following revelations about sexually explicit texts he sent to women outside his marriage. His wife had flagged the messages to his Senate campaign.

The scandal represents another challenge for Platner's bid to unseat Senator Susan Collins, a race Democrats view as central to their efforts to control Congress. Despite the controversy, Democratic leadership has continued to express support for his candidacy.

cards.headline: Thousands of sailors remain trapped by Strait of Hormuz blockade
cards.teaser: Around 20,000 seafarers have been stranded in the Iran war zone for months with no clear end in sight.
cards.body:
Approximately 20,000 seafarers remain trapped aboard vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, unable to transit the waterway due to the ongoing blockade. The sailors have been stranded for months in what has become an extended crisis in the strategic shipping lane.

Crew members report the prolonged uncertainty has created significant stress and exhaustion. The seafarers remain in the war zone with no clear timeline for when conditions might allow them to leave the area.

cards.headline: Bear attacks four workers at Japanese steel factory
cards.teaser: The bear injured four people and remains loose within the factory compound.
cards.body:
A bear injured four people in an attack at a steel works facility in Japan on Tuesday. The animal entered the factory compound and confronted employees before the incident occurred.

The bear remained at large within the factory grounds as authorities worked to locate and contain it.

hero.headline: Federal Reserve Chair Warsh Hires Conservative Policy Veterans as First Advisers
hero.body:
Kevin Warsh officially became chair of the Federal Reserve on May 14, taking control of one of the most influential positions in the U.S. government at a moment of intense scrutiny over the central bank's independence. The Senate confirmed Warsh in a 54-45 vote split largely along party lines, with Democrat John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voting with Republicans. This marked the most divisive Fed chair confirmation in history.

Warsh announced his first personnel decisions by appointing two conservative policy veterans as interim advisers. Paul Winfree, who contributed to Project 2025 (a conservative policy document), and another adviser named Heil join the Fed leadership. The appointments signal a significant shift in the ideological direction of the central bank under the new administration.

The 54-year-old economist and former Wall Street banker previously served as a Federal Reserve governor from 2006 to 2011, when he earned a reputation as an "inflation hawk" for advocating higher interest rates to combat rising prices. He left the Fed board partly due to disagreements over the central bank's post-financial crisis stimulus policies. Trump ultimately chose Jerome Powell for the top Fed job in 2018, a decision Trump now calls "a really big mistake."

Warsh takes the helm as the Fed faces pressure from the Trump administration to lower interest rates. Inflation currently stands at 3.8%, complicating any push for rate cuts. The Fed controls interest rates, which determine borrowing costs. Higher rates cool spending and reduce prices but risk increasing unemployment. Lower rates can stimulate the economy but may push prices higher.

At his Senate confirmation hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and "take politics out of monetary policy and monetary policy out of politics." However, he refused to answer whether Trump lost the 2020 election, raising concerns among Democrats. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate banking committee, criticized his nomination, saying Trump selected Warsh to be his "sock puppet" to control interest rates. She warned that "Warsh's confirmation equals another step in Trump's attempt to take over the Fed."

Fetterman, the lone Democrat supporting Warsh, said he believes the new chair will be "transparent and responsive to Congress and the public" and praised Warsh's promise to maintain Fed independence in setting rates.

The appointments of conservative policy experts represent a departure from recent Fed staffing patterns. Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, whose term ended when Warsh took over, announced he would remain on the Fed board as a voting governor, citing ongoing White House scrutiny of the central bank's headquarters renovations. Powell later called this scrutiny "pretext" for pressure to lower rates and warned that political interference could permanently damage public trust in the Fed.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over Wind Farm Payment
cards.teaser: A coalition of states filed suit challenging a government deal that paid nearly $1 billion to halt an offshore wind project.
cards.body:
Seven states sued the Trump administration over a deal that paid a French company approximately $1 billion to stop building offshore wind farms. The lawsuit was filed by New York and six other states challenging the agreement with TotalEnergies.

The states argue the deal undermines renewable energy development and represents an improper use of federal funds to block clean energy infrastructure.

cards.headline: Treasury Sanctions Iran's Largest Cryptocurrency Exchange
cards.teaser: The United States imposed sanctions on Nobitex and other Iranian crypto platforms over links to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
cards.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, citing alleged connections to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The action targeted the platform along with other Iranian crypto services.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the United States seized approximately $1 billion in Iranian cryptocurrency holdings as part of the enforcement operation.

cards.headline: CBS Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: The network dismissed the longtime journalist after he criticized show leadership during a staff meeting.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a longtime 60 Minutes correspondent and former anchor of the CBS Evening News. The dismissal followed a heated staff meeting on Monday morning where Pelley sharply criticized the network's leadership and recent personnel decisions.

Pelley objected to CBS News management's decision to terminate the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. During the meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley directly attacked Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief, over the restructuring of the program.

cards.headline: Colorado Tightens Regulations on Uber and Lyft
cards.teaser: The state enacted a law increasing scrutiny of ride-hailing companies following reports about sexual assault disclosures.
cards.body:
Colorado enacted legislation that increases regulatory oversight of Uber and Lyft. The law cited a New York Times investigation that found Uber received reports of sexual assault or sexual misconduct far more frequently than the company had publicly disclosed.

The new regulations impose tighter scrutiny on how ride-hailing companies handle and report safety incidents. The legislation aims to increase transparency and accountability for platforms operating in Colorado.

cards.headline: Shipping Vessel Hit by Projectiles in Iraqi Port
cards.teaser: A Mediterranean Shipping Company vessel was struck by two projectiles, highlighting ongoing risks to commercial shipping.
cards.body:
A Mediterranean Shipping Company vessel came under attack in an Iraqi port when it was struck by two projectiles. The incident highlights the ongoing risks facing commercial shipping in the region.

The attack occurred as the United States and Iran engage in negotiations aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The incident underscores the security challenges that persist for maritime operations even as diplomatic efforts work to ease tensions and restore normal shipping activity in the critical waterway.

cards.headline: Ulta Beauty Raises Earnings Outlook After Strong Quarter
cards.teaser: The cosmetics retailer exceeded Wall Street expectations and increased its full-year profit forecast.
cards.body:
Ulta Beauty reported fiscal first-quarter results that beat analyst expectations, prompting the company to raise its earnings outlook for the full year. Revenue increased across sales channels and major product categories.

Shares of the beauty retailer rose following the earnings announcement. The company delivered gains in both revenue and profit, reflecting growth in consumer spending on cosmetics and beauty products despite broader economic uncertainty.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches Scout AI assistant designed to work continuously across tasks
hero.body:
Microsoft has released Scout, an AI assistant that operates continuously to help users manage work tasks and information. The company describes Scout as a personal agent that remains active in the background, drawing comparisons to an executive assistant.

Internal documents obtained by 404 Media reveal that Microsoft aims to make users dependent on the new tool. The documents state the company wants to "make people addicted" to Scout, according to the reporting. Microsoft has positioned Scout as an always-on assistant that can handle various workplace functions.

The launch represents Microsoft's latest effort to integrate AI capabilities into productivity workflows. Scout builds on the company's existing AI investments, including its partnership with OpenAI. The assistant is designed to work alongside users rather than requiring them to switch between applications or manually trigger functions.

Microsoft announced Scout at its Build developer conference, where the company also introduced several other AI-focused initiatives. The company unveiled new AI models intended to reduce its reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. Microsoft also presented Work IQ APIs and demonstrated Linux tools for Windows developers, along with an RTX Spark desktop for development work.

The Scout launch coincides with Microsoft testing a wearable AI device aimed at office workers, according to BBC reporting. The combination of software and potential hardware products indicates Microsoft is pursuing multiple approaches to embedding AI assistants into daily work routines. The company has framed these developments as part of a new era of AI-driven devices and services at its annual developer conference.

cards.headline: Microsoft testing wearable AI device for workplace use
cards.teaser: The company is developing hardware to accompany its AI software push.
cards.body:
Microsoft is testing a wearable AI gadget designed for office workers, according to BBC reporting. The device represents a hardware component of the company's broader AI strategy.

The wearable comes as Microsoft introduces multiple AI products at its Build developer conference. The company is exploring how AI assistants can integrate into daily work through both software and physical devices worn by users.

cards.headline: Microsoft unveils Android-based operating system built for AI agents
cards.teaser: Project Solara prioritizes AI agents over traditional applications.
cards.body:
Microsoft has announced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed around AI agents rather than traditional apps. The platform represents a shift in how operating systems organize and deliver functionality to users.

The project reflects Microsoft's acknowledgment that it missed opportunities in the app-driven mobile era. By building an OS centered on agents, the company is attempting to establish a presence in what it views as the next computing paradigm.

cards.headline: Insomniac Games shows new Wolverine gameplay at PlayStation event
cards.teaser: The studio revealed violent action sequences for its upcoming Marvel game.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games presented new gameplay footage for Marvels Wolverine during PlayStation's State of Play presentation. The trailer showcased combat sequences that emphasized the character's brutal fighting style.

The gameplay reveal included story details about the upcoming title from the studio behind the recent Spider-Man games. Multiple outlets described the violence level as notably high, fitting the Wolverine character. PlayStation also showed other titles during the State of Play event.

cards.headline: Ubisoft announces Rayman Legends remake for October release
cards.teaser: Rayman Legends Retold will transform the 2D platformer into a 3D game.
cards.body:
Ubisoft has announced Rayman Legends Retold, a 3D remake of Rayman Legends set to launch on October 1. Game Informer reported playing the game for two hours and described it as a remake of what many consider the best Rayman title.

The game will release on PlayStation 5, according to the PlayStation Blog. Ubisoft is also releasing Rayman Origins: Enhanced Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, expanding the availability of classic Rayman titles across current platforms.

cards.headline: Apple previews iOS 27 features ahead of developer conference
cards.teaser: The company is preparing major Siri and AI updates for its June event.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to unveil iOS 27 at its Worldwide Developers Conference on June 8. Bloomberg reported the company plans to overhaul Siri and introduce new AI features in the operating system update.

Apple has released promotional materials for WWDC with the tagline "All Systems Glow," along with playlists and wallpapers. The event is expected to include multiple announcements that analysts believe could impact the company's stock performance. The conference comes at a time when Apple is focusing heavily on AI capabilities.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera seeks funding at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The company is raising $300 million despite operating at a loss.
cards.body:
Cyera is nearing completion of a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners that would value the cybersecurity company at $12 billion. The valuation represents 80 times the company's annual recurring revenue.

Cyera is currently operating at a loss, making the high valuation multiple notable in the current funding environment. The company focuses on cybersecurity services and has attracted significant investor interest despite its financial performance.

hero.headline: Falcons sign wide receiver Drake London to four-year, $141 million extension
hero.body:
The Atlanta Falcons and wide receiver Drake London agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $141 million, according to London's agent. The deal secures the former first-round pick through the 2029 season and makes him one of the highest-paid receivers in the NFL.

London, who entered the league as the eighth overall pick in the 2022 draft, has developed into a cornerstone of Atlanta's offense. The extension reflects the team's confidence in the 24-year-old as a long-term building block alongside quarterback Desmond Ridder. The contract places London among the top-paid players at his position, though he falls just outside the top five in average annual value.

The extension has immediate ripple effects across the league's wide receiver market. Multiple reports indicate that players including Puka Nacua and George Pickens are among the top candidates for their own contract extensions following London's deal. The agreement also affected existing contract rankings, with the Steelers' DK Metcalf dropping out of the top five highest-paid receivers at his position.

The Falcons made London their first selection in 2022 after trading longtime franchise quarterback Matt Ryan to Indianapolis. London caught passes from multiple quarterbacks during his first three seasons as the team worked to stabilize its offense. His production improved steadily each year, helping justify the organization's investment in him as a centerpiece of their receiving corps.

The deal addresses one of Atlanta's key offseason priorities by locking down a young offensive weapon before he reached free agency. London still has one year remaining on his rookie contract, meaning the extension will keep him in Atlanta through at least six total seasons. The Falcons completed the agreement during the early stages of their offseason program, providing clarity on a major roster decision well before training camp.

cards.headline: Liverpool reach agreement with Andoni Iraola to replace Arne Slot as head coach
cards.teaser: Liverpool agreed to terms with manager Andoni Iraola following the dismissal of Arne Slot.
cards.body:
Liverpool have reached a verbal agreement with Andoni Iraola to become their next head coach, following Arne Slot's departure from the club.

Iraola, the former Bournemouth manager, will take charge of the Premier League side as it seeks a new direction under fresh leadership.

cards.headline: Manchester United agree to pay Atalanta $35 million for midfielder Ederson
cards.teaser: Manchester United finalized a transfer fee with Atalanta for Brazilian midfielder Ederson.
cards.body:
Manchester United have agreed a £35 million deal with Atalanta to sign Brazilian midfielder Ederson, with the 26-year-old set to become Michael Carrick's first signing as permanent manager. Personal terms have been agreed on a contract running until 2030.

Ederson was identified by Carrick and director of football Jason Wilcox as a replacement for Casemiro, who departed after his contract expired. The move represents United's opening business in the transfer window as they strengthen their midfield.

cards.headline: Former Iowa State forward Milan Momcilovic commits to Kentucky basketball
cards.teaser: Kentucky secured a commitment from transfer forward Milan Momcilovic, who is scheduled to arrive on campus this weekend.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic committed to play basketball at Kentucky after transferring from Iowa State. The forward is scheduled to arrive at the university on Saturday to join the Wildcats program.

Momcilovic chose Kentucky over Louisville in what became a competitive recruiting battle between the two programs. The addition of the former Iowa State player represents a significant transfer portal acquisition for Kentucky as the team builds its roster for next season.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev advances to French Open semifinals with quarterfinal victory
cards.teaser: Alexander Zverev defeated teenager Rafael Jodar in the French Open quarterfinals to continue his pursuit of a first Grand Slam title.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev advanced to the French Open semifinals with a comprehensive quarterfinal victory over teenage opponent Rafael Jodar. The German player's dominant performance keeps his pursuit of a maiden Grand Slam title alive at Roland Garros.

Zverev will face Jakub Mensik in the semifinals as he aims to reach the championship match. The win positions him two victories away from claiming his first major tournament title.

cards.headline: Eagles receiver A.J. Brown selects jersey number one with Patriots
cards.teaser: A.J. Brown chose to wear number one after joining the Patriots, despite receiving approval from Julian Edelman to wear number 11.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation about his future. The move reunites Brown with coach Mike Vrabel and comes after the receiver grew frustrated with Philadelphia. The Eagles received a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 in the deal.

Brown selected No. 1 for his Patriots jersey, declining the opportunity to wear No. 11 despite receiving permission from former Patriots receiver Julian Edelman. The trade sparked mixed reactions among Eagles players during organized team activities.

cards.headline: England coach Charlotte Edwards praises Heather Knight ahead of T20 World Cup
cards.teaser: England head coach Charlotte Edwards expressed confidence in former captain Heather Knight's spot on the World Cup roster.
cards.body:
Charlotte Edwards has backed Heather Knight's place in the England squad ahead of the T20 World Cup, expressing confidence in the former captain's resilience. The head coach said she never doubted Knight's selection for the tournament.

Knight's form has improved at a crucial moment, with England preparing for their World Cup opener against Sri Lanka on 12 June. She featured in England's recent T20 series victory over India, forming a 137-run partnership with Alice Capsey in a successful run chase at Taunton.

hero.headline: Actor Nick Pasqual Sentenced to 32 Years to Life for Stabbing Ex-Girlfriend
hero.teaser: The How I Met Your Mother actor received the sentence for the attempted murder of his estranged girlfriend.
hero.body:
Nick Pasqual, an actor and producer who appeared in How I Met Your Mother, was sentenced to 32 years to life in prison for the attempted murder of his ex-girlfriend. Pasqual stabbed the woman, who worked as a makeup artist, more than 20 times in the attack.

The sentence was handed down following Pasqual's conviction on attempted murder charges. The severity of the attack, which involved multiple stab wounds, formed the basis for the lengthy prison term that includes the possibility of life imprisonment.

cards.headline: CBS Fires Scott Pelley After Clash With New 60 Minutes Leadership
cards.teaser: The veteran journalist was terminated following a public dispute with the show's newly appointed executive producer.
cards.body:
CBS News has terminated veteran 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley following a heated confrontation during a staff meeting on Monday. Pelley publicly criticized the network's recent decision to fire the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega as part of a management overhaul.

The dispute occurred during a meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle. Pelley directed his complaints at editorial chief Bari Weiss, whose leadership has driven significant changes at CBS News. The network determined it could not continue working with Pelley following the clash.

cards.headline: Grammy Winner Peabo Bryson Dies at 75
cards.teaser: Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning singer known for his romantic ballads and iconic Disney duets, has died at age 75.
cards.body:
Peabo Bryson, the two-time Grammy-winning R&B singer, died Tuesday at age 75, days after suffering a stroke, his family announced.

Bryson was best known for his iconic Disney duets, including the Oscar-winning "Beauty and the Beast" with Celine Dion and "A Whole New World" with Regina Belle from Aladdin. His distinctive voice on these songs introduced him to generations of listeners and cemented his place in pop music history.

cards.headline: NBC Cancels The Hunting Party After Two Seasons
cards.teaser: The crime drama starring Melissa Roxburgh will be shopped to other outlets following its cancellation.
cards.body:
NBC has canceled The Hunting Party after two seasons. The crime drama, which starred Melissa Roxburgh as FBI profiler Rebecca "Bex" Henderson, concluded with its final episode on May 7.

The show followed Henderson and her investigative team as they tracked dangerous criminals. According to reports, the series will be shopped to other networks and streaming platforms.

cards.headline: Ernest Chambers, Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour Showrunner, Dies at 97
cards.teaser: The veteran television writer and producer died at his Los Angeles home following a brief illness.
cards.body:
Ernest Chambers, the writer and producer known for his work on The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour and other variety shows, died on May 28 at his home in Los Angeles. He was 97. Chambers had been suffering from a brief illness before his death.

Over his 50-year career in television, Chambers produced, wrote, and executive produced more than 1,000 hours of programming. His work on variety shows earned him 11 Emmy nominations throughout his career, establishing him as a significant figure in television comedy production.

cards.headline: JioHotstar Recruits for 75 AI Positions in Tech Expansion
cards.teaser: India's largest streaming platform is building a dedicated artificial intelligence division across multiple departments.
cards.body:
India's largest streaming platform, JioHotstar, is hiring more than 75 artificial intelligence professionals to establish a dedicated AI division. The recruitment drive spans engineering, production automation, and creative technology roles.

The company aims to leverage India's multilingual capabilities and technical talent to fuel global expansion. By developing homegrown AI technology, JioHotstar is positioning itself as a major player in the competitive streaming market while building indigenous technological infrastructure.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Returns for Eighth Season
cards.teaser: The reality dating show begins its latest season with a new cast and streaming availability.
cards.body:
Love Island USA is back for season 8 with a fresh cast of contestants ready to compete in the reality dating competition. The new season is available to stream, allowing viewers to watch episodes through various streaming apps.

Fans can tune in to follow the contestants as they navigate relationships and challenges throughout the season. The show continues to draw audiences to its signature format that has made it a popular fixture in reality television.

hero.headline: U.S. shoots down Iranian missiles and drones, strikes targets near Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
U.S. forces shot down multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones and conducted strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to attempted attacks across the Middle East. U.S. Central Command said all Iranian ballistic missiles failed to hit their intended targets, marking a significant escalation in military tensions between the two nations.

According to CENTCOM, two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart during flight, while three missiles launched at Bahrain were intercepted by U.S. and Bahrain air defense forces. The U.S. military characterized these actions as defensive operations necessary to protect American forces and regional partners.

The strikes on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz followed the attempted Iranian attacks. The confrontation extended beyond direct military exchanges, with American forces also responding to Iranian threats aimed at regional allies. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway through which much of the world's oil passes.

In a separate incident, an F-35C fighter jet from the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone in the Arabian Sea. According to Captain Tim Hawkins, a navy spokesperson at Central Command, the drone was "aggressively" approaching the carrier "with unclear intent" when it was intercepted. "An F-35C fighter jet from Abraham Lincoln shot down the Iranian drone in self-defence and to protect the aircraft carrier and personnel on board," Hawkins said. No U.S. service members were harmed or equipment damaged.

Also on Tuesday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards harassed a U.S.-flagged merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Two IRGC boats and an Iranian Mohajer drone approached the M/V Stena Imperative at high speeds and threatened to board the tanker, according to military officials.

These military confrontations come as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran have stalled. However, there are signs negotiations may resume. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian announced he had instructed the country's foreign minister to "pursue fair and equitable negotiations" with the U.S., marking a potential shift in Tehran's position. The White House confirmed that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff plans to hold talks with Iranian officials later in the week.

The escalation represents the latest in a series of military exchanges in the Middle East involving American and Iranian forces. U.S. Central Command oversees military operations across the Middle East and Central Asia, including forces stationed in Kuwait, Bahrain, and other regional bases that came under threat from the Iranian attacks. The deterioration in relations underscores the fragile security situation in the region amid continued tensions over nuclear negotiations and American military presence near Iranian waters.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use Republican-favored congressional map for midterms
cards.teaser: The Court cleared the way for a map with six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that Alabama can use a redrawn congressional map for the 2026 midterm elections featuring six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district. The decision came through an emergency ruling.

The new map eliminates one of Alabama's two majority-Black congressional districts, dealing a significant blow to Black voters while benefiting Republicans. This ruling represents another major victory for the GOP following the court's earlier decision that made it substantially harder to win Voting Rights Act claims.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The former Biden administration official previously served as Interior Secretary before entering the gubernatorial race.

Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor if elected in November. She will face the Republican nominee in the general election for the position.

cards.headline: California governor primary underway with five major candidates
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra face Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California voters are choosing a Democrat to replace outgoing Gov. Gavin Newsom in a race that will determine who leads the nation's fourth-largest economy. Xavier Becerra, the establishment favorite and former Health and Human Services Secretary, is competing against billionaire Tom Steyer and Rep. Katie Porter for the Democratic nomination. Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are also on the ballot.

As polls closed Tuesday, Becerra and Steyer led among Democratic candidates. California's mail-in voting system means final results will take days or weeks to tabulate, as ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive at county election offices through June 9.

cards.headline: Canada urges renewal of North American free-trade agreement
cards.teaser: Canadian officials sent a letter to U.S. and Mexican trade representatives calling for a 16-year extension.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal in a letter from Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc to his U.S. and Mexican counterparts. The request comes amid economic and political pressure from the Trump administration.

The three countries must decide on the future of their trade relationship, which currently governs commerce between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

cards.headline: Ashley Hinson wins Republican Senate primary in Iowa
cards.teaser: The GOP congresswoman will face Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek for the seat held by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst.
cards.body:
Rep. Ashley Hinson won the Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Iowa and will face state Rep. Josh Turek in the general election for retiring Sen. Joni Ernst's seat. Hinson, a former reporter and state lawmaker who has represented Iowa's northeastern corner in Congress since 2021, defeated former state Rep. Jim Carlin for the GOP nomination.

Turek, a two-time Paralympic gold medalist, is the Democratic nominee for the fall election. Both candidates are competing to fill Ernst's Senate seat as she steps down.

cards.headline: Zach Nunn and Sarah Trone Garriott to face off in Iowa's 3rd District
cards.teaser: The Republican congressman and Democratic state senator both ran unopposed in their primaries.
cards.body:
GOP Rep. Zach Nunn and state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott will face each other in Iowa's 3rd Congressional District in November. Both candidates ran unopposed in their party primaries.

Nunn is a member of the Iowa Air National Guard and previously served in the Iowa House before winning election to Congress. Trone Garriott currently serves in the Iowa state Senate.
